title: Extending functions from a quasi-compact flat monomorphism
statement: Let $j:Z\to Y$ be a quasi-compact flat monomorphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-flat-morphism] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with $Z$ quasi-compact and $Y$ quasi-separated. Quasi-compact means that every open cover has a finite subcover; for a morphism it means that inverse images of affine opens are quasi-compact. Quasi-separated means that intersections of affine opens are quasi-compact. Monomorphism means that postcomposition by $j$ is injective on $\operatorname{Hom}(W,Z)$ for every scheme $W$. Put $E=j(|Z|)$. Then $E$ is stable under generalization: if $e\in E$ and $e\in\overline{\{y\}}$, then $y\in E$. For every $s\in\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ there are a quasi-compact open subscheme $V\subseteq Y$ containing $E$ [def-weil-open-immersion] and $t\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ such that $j_V^*(t)=s$, where $j_V:Z\to V$ is the factorization of $j$ through this open. No finite-presentation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Propositions 1.1 and 1.2(i), printed pp.1–2; Proposition 2.3(i), printed pp.4–5, applied to the induced ringed subspace E and its whole quasi-compact open. Online primary scan read; local archive WANTED.

proof.text: Apply the ringed-image theorem to $j$: with $i:E\hookrightarrow |Y|$, it identifies $Z$ canonically with $(E,i^{-1}\mathcal O_Y)$ over $Y$, and states that $E$ is stable under generalization and retrocompact. This proves the first assertion. The space $E$ is quasi-compact, since it is homeomorphic to the quasi-compact space $Z$. Write $\sigma\in\Gamma(E,i^{-1}\mathcal O_Y)$ for the section corresponding to $s$. If $E=\varnothing$, take $V=\varnothing$ and its unique section, so henceforth suppose $E\ne\varnothing$.

source.place: Propositions 1.1 and 1.2(i), printed pp.1–2; reduction before Proposition 2.3(i).

proof.text: For each $e\in E$, the inverse-image stalk theorem gives a neighbourhood $N_e\subseteq Y$ and $a_e\in\Gamma(N_e,\mathcal O_Y)$ whose image has germ $\sigma_e$. By the germ-equality description of stalks, the induced section and $\sigma$ agree on an open neighbourhood of $e$ in $E\cap N_e$. Write that neighbourhood as the trace of an open of $Y$ and choose an affine open $U_e$ inside it containing $e$, using the affine-open basis. Set $s_e=a_e|_{U_e}$. Thus $s_e$ induces $\sigma$ on $E\cap U_e$. Quasi-compactness of $E$ selects finitely many of these affine opens $U_1,\ldots,U_n$ covering $E$, with sections $s_1,\ldots,s_n$. Put $U_0=\bigcup_{a=1}^nU_a$; it is quasi-compact, being a finite union of affine opens, each quasi-compact by the affine-scheme theorem. Its affine-open intersections are those in $Y$, so $U_0$ is quasi-separated. The qcqs-scheme theorem therefore makes $|U_0|$ spectral.

source.place: Proposition 2.3(i), printed pp.4–5, finite local representatives and gluing; primary Numdam scan read online, local archive WANTED.

proof.text: For each pair $a,b$, let $A_{ab}=U_a\cap U_b$, which is quasi-compact by the quasi-separated-intersection theorem. Retrocompactness of $E$ makes $E\cap A_{ab}$ quasi-compact. At every $e\in E\cap A_{ab}$ the two induced sections equal $\sigma$, so their germs in $(i^{-1}\mathcal O_Y)_e$ agree. Injectivity of the inverse-image stalk isomorphism implies $(s_a)_e=(s_b)_e$ in $\mathcal O_{Y,e}$. The stalk definition gives a neighbourhood in $A_{ab}$ on which $s_a=s_b$; refine it to an affine open. Select finitely many such affine neighbourhoods covering $E\cap A_{ab}$ and let $W_{ab}$ be their union. Then $W_{ab}\subseteq A_{ab}$ is quasi-compact open, contains $E\cap A_{ab}$, and $s_a|_{W_{ab}}=s_b|_{W_{ab}}$ by locality of the structure sheaf. If $E\cap A_{ab}=\varnothing$, use $W_{ab}=\varnothing$.

source.place: Proposition 2.3(i), printed pp.4–5, finite local representatives and gluing; primary Numdam scan read online, local archive WANTED.

proof.text: Work in the spectral space $|U_0|$. Both $A_{ab}$ and $W_{ab}$ are quasi-compact opens and hence retrocompact there. Consequently $F_{ab}=A_{ab}\setminus W_{ab}$ is constructible: it is one of the defining differences of retrocompact opens. The finite union $F=\bigcup_{a,b}F_{ab}$ is constructible by the Boolean-algebra clause of the constructible-subset definition, and $F\cap E=\varnothing$ by the choice of $W_{ab}$.

source.place: Proposition 2.3(i), printed pp.4–5, finite local representatives and gluing; primary Numdam scan read online, local archive WANTED.

proof.text: Let $\overline F$ denote closure in $U_0$. If $e\in E\cap\overline F$, apply the spectral proconstructible-closure theorem to the singleton family with member $F$: there is $f\in F$ with $e\in\overline{\{f\}}$. The generalization stability of $E$ then forces $f\in E$, contradicting $F\cap E=\varnothing$. Thus $O=U_0\setminus\overline F$ is open in $Y$ and contains $E$. For each $e\in E$, choose an affine open of $Y$ containing $e$ inside $O$. A finite subcover of $E$ exists; let $V$ be its union. Then $V$ is quasi-compact open, $E\subseteq V\subseteq O$, and $V\cap F_{ab}=\varnothing$ for every pair.

source.place: Proposition 2.3(i), proof using Lemma 2.2; the constructible-avoidance inference is expanded using Stacks Tag 0903, topology.tex, lemma-constructible-stable-specialization-closed (1).

proof.text: The opens $V\cap U_a$ cover $V$. On an overlap, $V\cap U_a\cap U_b\subseteq W_{ab}$ because $V$ misses $F_{ab}$. Hence the sections $s_a|_{V\cap U_a}$ agree on every overlap. The sheaf axiom for $\mathcal O_Y$ glues them uniquely to $t\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$. Since $j(|Z|)\subseteq V$, the open-factorization theorem gives $j_V:Z\to V$. On $j^{-1}(U_a)$, its pullback of $t$ equals the pullback of $s_a$, which is $s$ by the ringed-image identification and the construction in step 2. These opens cover $Z$, so the sheaf uniqueness axiom gives $j_V^*(t)=s$.

source.place: Proposition 2.3(i), printed pp.4–5, finite local representatives and gluing; primary Numdam scan read online, local archive WANTED.

tool_uses.why: Canonical stalk isomorphism for ordinary topological inverse image, including its unit/germ formula; generic tool for the induced ringed subspace, not a replacement for the unit route.
Affine refinement of neighbourhoods and finite quasi-compact neighbourhood selection; generic scheme topology tool.
Spectrality of the finite union of affine opens, needed to apply the constructible closure theorem.
Quasi-compactness of overlaps under the actual quasi-separated hypothesis; no affine-overlap assumption.
Quasi-compact opens of the spectral neighbourhood are retrocompact, making the finite bad sets constructible.
Generic spectral closure theorem: closure points of a constructible bad set specialize from that set; it supplies precisely Raynaud Lemma 2.2 avoidance.
Factor the original morphism through the constructed open V; generic open-subscheme universal property.
Affine neighbourhoods are quasi-compact; finite unions used for U_0, W_ab and V are therefore quasi-compact. This generic scheme fact is not a route change.

The statement is kept: a quasi-compact flat monomorphism j:Z→Y with Z quasi-compact and Y quasi-separated; E=j(Z) is generalization-stable, and every global section extends to a quasi-compact open V containing E. It holds on test cases: the localization S^-1A, Spec O_{Y,y}, two minimal primes of k[x,y]/(xy) with section (1,0) extending on Y minus the origin, E empty, j surjective. Step 1: lem-sfb-qc-flat-monomorphism-ringed-image (same unit, unsplit, no cycle) gives the identification with the ringed subspace, generalization stability and retrocompactness. Steps 2–3: the inverse-image stalk representative, germ equality, the affine basis and the 'quasi-separated implies quasi-compact intersection' node (no overlap is assumed affine, so E1 is avoided) give finitely many charts U_a and agreement opens W_ab. Retrocompactness makes E∩A_ab quasi-compact. Step 4 (elementary): F_ab=A_ab minus W_ab is constructible in the spectral space U_0 by the retrocompact-iff-quasi-compact node and the definition. Step 5: the closure node with a singleton family (Stacks 0903(1), topology.tex l.4461, checked) plus generalization stability shows the closure of F misses E; the specialization direction is correct. Step 6: gluing on V∩U_a, the open-subscheme factorization, and pullback compared on j^-1(U_a). No new nodes. No duplicate found among spectral-limit-sheaf-sections, h0-spectral-closed-restriction, generalizing-subset-affine-envelope and spectral-generalizations-of-quasi-compact.
